newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cement price war seen bashing Apasco Q2 net income.
newsitem.headline: Cement price war seen bashing Apasco Q2 net income.

text.p: Second quarter net earnings at cement maker Apasco are expected to swoon compared to the year-ago quarter, partially due to a price war, analysts said.
"This is the first time that Apasco is losing a price war," said Gordon Lee of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, referring to the weakness of cement prices and the rough competition it has spawned.
A survey by Reuters of six industry analysts forecast earnings per share of 0.577 peso for the second quarter -- a drastic fall from 10.7 pesos last year.
Revenues, however, are expected to rise to 1.092 billion pesos, up slightly, up from the 1.068 billion inflation-adjusted sales of the second quarter last year, analysts said.

"They are going to report a real increase in sales, but the profits will be lower because in the second quarter (last year) prices per tonne (of cement) were high and after that began to fall," said Gerardo Saenz, an analyst with OBSA-Serfin.
Operating profits are seen falling to 207.4 million pesos in the second quarter this year from 310.6 million pesos in the same quarter a year earlier.

Analysts said, however, that compared to the first quarter numbers, Apasco's second quarter would show a grudging improvement from net earnings of 0.28 peso per share. The survey of analysts found expectations of a rise in revenues of 28.2 percent in the second quarter compared to the first quarter.
